fns.desc: If a peer method receives an EAP-pwd request with the fragmentation LENGTH bit set but the MORE bit clear (and in_frag_pos still 0), data->inbuf is allocated at :987 but never freed on this call (the :1064 free is gated on in_frag_pos!=0, which stays 0 here); it lingers until eap_pwd_deinit(), and a subsequent LENGTH-bit request while it's still set hits the :981 guard and returns without freeing it either. Session-scoped resource growth from a malformed/hostile EAP server, not a per-call leak.
